notes: Celgene paid $9B for Juno Therapeutics — autologous anti-CD19 CAR-T cell therapy Breyanzi (lisocabtagene maraleucel) for relapsed/refractory large B-cell lymphoma. Phase 2 at deal time; FDA-approved Feb 2021. Subsequent label expansions. Note: Celgene was itself acquired by BMS in Nov 2019 (~$74B), so Breyanzi is now a BMS commercial asset. Peak sales estimate $1.5B reflects Breyanzi-specific consensus, somewhat below Yescarta due to its later launch and the dueling-CAR-T market dynamic.
selection_rationale: Second canonical autologous CD19 CAR-T M&A. Phase 2 at deal time provides a useful pre-approval benchmark for the cell-therapy cohort (vs Kite's post-approval framing). The Celgene→BMS rollup is a real-world wrinkle; for cohort accounting we use the original Celgene-paid $9B as the deal value.
source: Celgene press release Jan 22 2018; Juno SEC filings; FDA approval letter Feb 5 2021.
